thread:
sam: Aegis dedicated pool is getting sustained 429s since ~03:10 UTC. TPS spike + burst credits drained fast. Anyone triaging?

maya: Yep, I'm on it. p95 latency up, admission controller started rejecting around 03:13.

oliver: Heads up: logs show token_bucket refill underrun. Quick prometheus check: 
```
sum by(pool) (burst_tokens_available{pool=\"aegis\"})
```
returns 0 from 03:14 to now.

zane: Looks like a noisy account — topk query shows one account consuming most tokens: 
```
topk(5, sum(rate(request_tokens_used[1m])) by (account))
# result snippet: acct_star_pay: 12k, acct-zen: 1.1k, others < 300
```

leo: Also saw billing/headroom sync job lagged ~4m around 03:08 (kicked off later). Could be refill credit reconciliation delay.

infra-bot: Autoscale events: pool aegs-dedicated scaled 2 -> 4 at 03:05 but admission controller still required burst credits to permit new inflight.

support-bot: Customer-facing errors: 429 with body: 'rate limit exceeded: burst tokens exhausted' reported by multiple endpoints.

sam: Immediate mitigation idea: temporarily bump burst_refill_rate or refill_amount for the pool so admissions stop rejecting while we investigate. Who can patch admission controller?

maya: I can do a short-lived change. Planning to set `burst_refill_rate=2.5` (was 1.0) for aegis pool to buy time. Applying now.

oliver: Good. Also consider pinning critical routes to standby capacity or fallback model to reduce token burn.

maya: Patch applied. Quick check cmd: 
```
kubectl exec -n infra admctl -- config get aegis | grep burst_refill_rate
```
shows 2.5. Monitoring...

zane: After the patch tokens are climbing, 429 rate dropping. Still see one tenant doing sustained fanout. We should add per-tenant shaping so a single account can't drain pool credits.

sam: Agreed. Short-term plan: 1) temp refill bump (done), 2) apply per-tenant soft cap on token rate during spikes, 3) reconcile billing/headroom job to avoid refill lag, 4) add alert when burst_tokens_available < 10%.

oliver: Repro steps (for eng-runtime): 
1) create dedicated pool with N=2 nodes and burst bucket size X
2) run synthetic client at 10k TPS hitting generation endpoint for 5m
3) watch `burst_tokens_available` drop and observe admission rejections/429s
4) confirm tokens recover when refill is increased or client slowed

maya: I'll open an eng ticket with those repro steps + logs. Also adding an emergency playbook entry to run `admctl config set <pool> burst_refill_rate` in incidents.

zane: I'll draft customer comms: short update saying we mitigated with a temporary config change, investigating root cause (noisy tenant + refill latency), expect PM and postmortem in 48h.

sam: Assigning postmortem to @oliver to capture timeline and proposed long-term fixes (per-tenant shaping, autoscale-slowpath detection, faster billing/headroom reconciliation). @zane please prepare the customer note.

oliver: Will do. I'll capture metrics (tokens, per-account token use, autoscale events) and propose circuit-breaker thresholds.

leo: Follow-up items for infra: add metric alert, consider increasing minimal prewarm credits for high-SLA customers, and add a noisy-tenant label so Ops can quickly throttle costly accounts.

maya: Ops note: avoid permanent high refill rates; that masks noisy tenants. Permanent fix should be shaping and better headroom guarantees.

sam: Thanks all. Current status: mitigated -> reduced 429s, ongoing follow-up tickets filed. Will update when we have PM + timeline. :thumbsup:
